maya: :eyes: Seeing a spike in p99 intra-cluster latency and packet loss for GPU inference pods across us-west-2a -> us-west-2b. Pods show TCP retransmits and RoCEv2 errors. Any recent network/kernel/CNI changes?

net-bot: network-monitor: BGP route-flap detected for v6 prefix 2600:1f14:abcd::/48 on bgp-peer igw-2 — affecting ~6 hosts.

ben: can you drop `ip -6 route` and `ip -6 neigh` from an affected node and confirm whether we upgraded calico or the kernel recently?

maya: pasted snippets from node-23: 
```
$ ip -6 route show table main
2600:1f14:abcd::/48 proto bird metric 20
fe80::/64 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 256
default via fe80::1 dev enp1s0f0 proto static metric 1024
```
and
```
$ ip -6 neigh show | grep 2600:1f14:abcd::a3
2600:1f14:abcd::a3 dev cali1234llllllllllll lladdr aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff REACHABLE
```
Also `dmesg` on several nodes shows repeated "IPv6: packet too big" messages and some RoCE driver warnings.

sofia: "Packet too big" -> classic PMTU fragmentation issue. Did calico change tunnel mode recently? IPIP/VXLAN add extra headers; if MTU mismatch + offloads it's a blackhole.

alex: we rolled kernel 6.2.15 to prod yesterday to pick up a RoCE bugfix. That kernel changed default GRO/GSO behavior on some NICs. If host offload cooperates poorly with calico tunnels, fragments can be generated or PTB messages not delivered. Check `ethtool -k` on cali interfaces.

maya: ethtool output snippet shows GRO: on, GSO: on on host, but cali interface shows offloads disabled. Observed PTB from a border router but the PTB source address didn't match the sender (asymmetric path). NDP entries also flip to wrong mac after a node failover (looks like proxying).

ben: if ICMPv6 PTB messages are dropped by some middlebox or get sent on a different path, TCP stalls. For RoCEv2 this breaks things earlier. Quick checks: `tcpdump -i cali+ "icmp6 && ip6[40] == 2"` to capture PTB, `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra` and `rp_filter` values. Also inspect BGP next-hops and ECMP hashing.

sofia: ran tcpdump — saw PTB from leaf-router-7 but the next-hop MAC resolves to a different node. We also use metalLB in BGP mode and recently enabled "external-ads"; possible FRR advertisement change or NDP proxy on switches rewriting macs.

alex: we've seen this pattern before: calico node-to-node encapsulation + kernel offload mismatch + BGP path asymmetry => PTB gets lost. IPIP/VXLAN reduce effective MTU (20-60 bytes depending), and if some hosts advertise wrong PMTU the sender never gets correct PTB. As immediate mitigations: reduce calico MTU, disable GRO/GSO on problem interfaces, and allow ICMPv6 PTB through ACLs.

maya: short-term plan: 1) set calico MTU to 1450 on affected nodes, 2) turn off GRO/GSO on cali interfaces (`ethtool -K caliXXXXX gro off gso off tso off`), 3) confirm PTB reachability, 4) move GPU pods to dedicated-us-east cluster for continuity. Patching kernel is medium-term. I'll open a network ticket to audit BGP/FRR and NDP proxy settings.

ben: please document the exact commands and a change window. Also check kube-proxy mode — ipvs has different conntrack behavior on dual-stack that can interact badly with fragmented IPv6.

maya: deploying the canary redirect to dedicated-us-east now (will affect some latency-sensitive traffic). Will post runbook once done. :handshake:

deploy-bot: canary-reroute: executed by maya at 1772129400 — 18 pods rerouted to dedicated-us-east.

sofia: follow-up: after lowering calico MTU and disabling GRO on cali interfaces p99 dropped back to baseline and RoCEv2 errors stopped. Still investigating root cause (likely BGP next-hop rewrite + kernel offload + encapsulation MTU). Will keep infra team assigned.
